partial: The restriction to asking only residents of Switzerland is not backed: the fund marks Canton required for everyone, and F-SC-017 says what applies to people living abroad (and residence versus work canton) is unclear.

partial: The cited facts never mention a pension fund canton question or say it is skipped for residents abroad and asked for residents in Switzerland (AC-02.2.2, AC-02.2.3), and the claim that source tax and HR receive the country of residence is not backed either.

partial: The cited facts leave open whether the canton means residence or work and what applies to people abroad (F-SC-006, F-SC-017), so asking only Swiss-resident employees and naming the item residence_canton is an unbacked assumption.

partial: AC-04.4.5 states that HR has checked the rules against Stefan, Maria and Tomás and that gaps go through OQ-05, but the facts only show HR hedging ('I think that's it') and say nothing about such a check or that handling; the other criteria are backed by F-TR-005/025/030/034/037/040.

Does 'first working day' mean the contractual start date or the first day the employee actually works? E.g. a contract starting 01.01.2027 (a public holiday; the spec uses it as an example) where the person first works on 04.01.2027 gives 01.01.2027 under one reading and 01.02.2027 under the other. The same applies to a start on the 1st that falls on a weekend. Which date do we ask for, and how do we word the question?

'Confirm' suggests the employee checks a date Lonio already has. Does Lonio get the contract start date from HR and show it for confirmation or correction, or does the employee type the date in from scratch? This changes the flow, and whether HR has to supply data first.

AC-01.2.4 / F-TR-019: what happens if the start date moves AFTER the employee has finished onboarding (Julia's case)? Can the employee (or HR) change the confirmed date later, and is the insurance start date then worked out again? Or does this feature only cover the date given during onboarding?

Which first working days are allowed? Can it be in the past (onboarding finished after the start), and how far in the future can it be? Should a weekend or public holiday be rejected or flagged? Without limits, a typo (wrong year) goes straight into a wrong insurance start date, which is exactly the incident this feature is meant to prevent.

How is 'country of residence' meant to be defined? The Notes say using the address country as the country of residence is 'confirmed by the product owner convention (G-09)', but G-09 is only 'Questionnaire language: English', so nothing confirms the inference. Which address should the employee give if the address HR posts documents to is not where they legally live? Examples: a weekly resident in Switzerland (Wochenaufenthalter) whose home is abroad, an employee with a second home, or an employee who moves around the start date. The answer decides whether one address is enough or we need a residence question or a separate postal address.

Is the house number really required for everyone? The spec says it is 'Always' required, but its own note says 'whether every address has a house number is not discussed'. Some rural or foreign addresses have no number, or use a building name. Should those employees be able to finish the step, for example by leaving the number empty or confirming 'no number'?

'No extra parts' (AC-02.1.2) rules out things like a c/o line, an apartment or flat number, or a second address line. Is that intended even when the post needs them to deliver (e.g. a new employee living c/o someone, or a large building abroad)? Or did HR only mean 'nothing beyond a normal envelope address'? This decides exactly which parts we collect.

AC-02.1.3 ('HR receives the complete home address' when 'the onboarding data is made available to the receiving parties') and AC-02.2.2 ('source tax and HR receive the country of residence') describe passing data on to other parties. out-of-scope.md (G-04) says that is a separate topic. What should these criteria be tested against in this feature? Should they be reworded to 'the information is collected and marked as needed by HR / source tax'?

What should happen if the employee goes back and changes the country after later steps were answered (e.g. Switzerland → Germany, or the reverse)? Should answers that no longer apply (nationality, canton, permit, spouse data) be discarded, which data minimisation (G-01) suggests? And should questions that now apply be asked again?

The goal says a registration is "never blocked by missing data", but the fund requires a canton for every employee and US-03.4 skips the canton for anyone living abroad (Germany, Liechtenstein). Until OQ-02 is answered, these registrations will be blocked. For now, should Lonio still let these employees complete the questionnaire, or should the case be marked as incomplete or flagged to HR? Or do we accept that the goal is not met for them yet? This is separate from OQ-02 itself, which asks what the canton means.

For employees living in Switzerland, the canton follows from the Swiss postcode and town they already give in FEAT-02. Guidance prefers deriving values over asking for them. Should the canton be derived from the address instead of asked? If it is still asked, what happens when the chosen canton does not match the postcode? Should it be checked, or accepted as entered?

Suppose an employee answers a dependent question and then changes the answer it depends on: civil status from Married to something else, or country from Switzerland to abroad. Should the spouse's date of birth or canton they already gave be discarded? Data minimisation (G-01) suggests yes, but the spec does not say.

Who makes the source tax decision: Lonio automatically, or HR? AC-04.1.1, AC-04.2.1 and AC-04.3.1 say 'HR uses it to decide', but US-04.4 and AC-04.4.1–4 say Lonio decides and that this gates the tariff questions straight away. If Lonio decides, can HR review or override it (for example in a case the rule does not cover, OQ-05) before the employee gets or skips the source tax step?

Does the spouse rule apply to anyone other than civil status 'Married'? Registered partners (e.g. Daniel), separated spouses and anyone else outside the pension fund's 4 values would currently go straight to 'subject'. OQ-03 raises this for source tax but is not linked to this feature. Should FEAT-04 wait for it, or ship treating only 'Married' as married?

The rule only needs to know whether someone is Swiss, holds a C permit or lives in Switzerland. Should Lonio ask for the full nationality (employee and spouse) and the spouse's full country of residence, or only 'Swiss yes/no' and 'lives in Switzerland yes/no'? The 'What?' rows say '(whether they hold a Swiss passport)' / '(whether they live in Switzerland)', but the ACs say 'asks for the nationality' and 'asks where the spouse lives'. Under data minimisation (G-01) the answer changes what we collect. Does HR need the actual nationality for anything else?

How should dual nationals be handled? Is someone who holds Swiss and another nationality treated as Swiss, both for the employee and for the spouse? This decides whether one nationality answer is enough or several are allowed.

Permit type is required for every non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland. What should an employee answer if their permit is still being applied for or has not been issued yet, or if they hold something that is not a residence permit (e.g. a short-term or asylum status)? Can they finish the questionnaire, and what does the rule decide for them? This goes beyond OQ-06, which only covers the list of permit types.

"they give the start date as currently agreed with Muster AG, as a full date in the form DD.MM.YYYY" - Sets the input format the employee must type. G-10 covers business wording for values in examples. The fund's DD.MM.YYYY requirement (F-SC-009) applies to the insurance start date sent to the fund, not to how the employee enters the first working day. How the date is entered (date picker, locale format) is a UI decision for engineering.
"When they reach the employment details" - Assumes a questionnaire step called 'employment details' that no source asks for. How the questions are split into steps is a design choice.

"When the onboarding data is made available to the receiving parties … Then HR receives the complete home address" - This describes how and when the system hands data over to recipients. Nobody asked for that behaviour here, and G-04 puts transmission out of scope. The business need is only that the address is collected once and is available for HR.

"and cannot complete the step while any of these five parts is empty" - This prescribes how the form behaves (blocking the step). The business requirement is only that all five parts are required. How completeness is enforced (blocking, warning, review before submitting) is a design decision.
"It depends on address_country from FEAT-02." - Uses an internal field id in business prose. The business term is "country of home address".
"naming the item residence_canton is an unbacked assumption" - Refers to an internal field or data-model name in the body text. What to call the field is an engineering decision.

"they are asked for their date of birth as a day, month and year (shown as DD.MM.YYYY, e.g. 14.02.1990)" - The fund's DD.MM.YYYY format is a constraint on the data delivered to the fund. Telling the questionnaire to ask for day, month and year as separate parts and to display them that way is an input and UI decision that belongs to engineering and design.

"Analyse the Zurich calculator and add its questions, asked only when subject_to_source_tax is true" - Uses an internal field id and a boolean value in prose. The business statement is 'asked only of employees subject to source tax'.

"Lonio asks for the employee's nationality, the employee must answer it, and HR uses it to decide" - Says how the decision is made (a question that HR then uses) instead of what outcome is needed. It also conflicts with US-04.4, where Lonio itself decides. This is a borderline case: how the decision is handled internally should be left to the design.

info.message: AC-01.1.3 talks about handing data on to HR and the pension fund, but G-04 / out-of-scope.md exclude transmission. What exactly do we build and test for AC-01.1.3? Does HR see the derived insurance start date, and where?
Should the derived insurance start date be shown to the employee (e.g. as information on the summary), or only to HR? AC-01.2.1 only says the employee is not asked for it.

AC-01.1.2 ('as currently agreed with Muster AG') cannot be checked by the system. Is it only guidance wording for the question (e.g. a hint that the date may have changed since the contract was signed)? If so, what should the text say?
AC-01.1.1 says the question appears 'when they reach the employment details'. No such step is defined in the shared files. Where does this question go in the order of the questionnaire?

Does the 1st-of-month rule apply to every employee, including re-hires, short or temporary contracts and people below the BVG thresholds? Or are some employees not registered with the fund at all, so no insurance start date is needed?

Which countries can the employee choose: any country in the world, or a limited list (e.g. Switzerland and neighbouring countries)? The examples confirm that Liechtenstein counts as 'abroad'. Is that confirmed by HR or the source tax office, given how closely Liechtenstein is tied to Switzerland?

Should address parts be checked for plausibility for the chosen country (e.g. a Swiss postcode must exist and match the town)? Or is any non-empty entry accepted? HR's need is mail that arrives, so wrong postcodes matter to them.
Does HR or the employer already know the employee's address before onboarding, so it could be pre-filled for the employee to confirm, or must the employee always type it in?

AC-02.2.4 only says the address step comes before the pension and source tax steps. Does it have to come at a particular place relative to FEAT-01 (first working day) or other steps, or is anything acceptable as long as it comes before the dependent steps?

Which names should the employee enter: the official names exactly as on their passport or ID, including all first names and middle names, or the name they use day to day? The fund's registration and later matching may depend on this, and it changes the question wording and help text.

Are there plausibility rules for the employee's date of birth and the spouse's date of birth? For example: not in the future, a minimum or maximum age for the employee, the spouse being an adult. Today the only rules are "not empty" and "a valid date", so a mistyped year would reach the fund.

AC-03.1.3 ("another part of the onboarding or another receiving party needs the same detail … not asked again") cannot be tested as written. Which other features or parties reuse name and date of birth? The information catalogue lists only the pension fund. What should the test check?

The title of AC-03.2.3 says civil status is reused "for source tax and HR", but its Then clause covers only source tax. Is there an HR reuse that needs its own acceptance criterion? If not, should "HR" be removed from the title?

Where in the questionnaire flow does the canton question go? FEAT-02 (AC-02.2.3) says employees living in Switzerland "continue to nationality and canton" straight after the address. FEAT-03 groups name and date of birth under "personal details" and civil status under "family details" but does not place the canton. Is there a required order across FEAT-02, FEAT-03 and FEAT-04?

'Lives in Switzerland' comes only from the country of the home address. What about weekly residents and others with two homes, e.g. a Swiss address during the week and a family home abroad? Which address should the employee give, and does HR accept that the rule follows it?

If the employee changes an earlier answer (address country, nationality, permit, civil status, spouse details) after the follow-up questions were answered, should the answers that are no longer needed be discarded (data minimisation), and should the source tax decision and the source tax step be recalculated? What happens to tariff answers already given if the employee turns out not to be subject?
Should the employee see the outcome (e.g. 'you are / are not subject to source tax'), or is it only stored for HR and the source tax step? No AC says who sees the decision or where.

AC-04.4.5 is a release precondition ('HR has checked the rules against real cases'), not behaviour we can test in the product, and its own trace check says the sources do not support it. Who signs this off, and is it a release gate for this feature or just part of resolving OQ-05?

Can a spouse who holds a C permit be living abroad (a C permit usually lapses after a long stay abroad)? If not, can we skip the residence question for C-permit spouses? Should the residence question be asked even when the spouse obviously lives with the employee?

uncited_units.text: HR meeting transcript Everyone and everything here is fictional. Anna is the HR manager at Muster AG. Leo works in product at Lonio.
Can you hear me okay? You're a bit quiet.
Is this better? I'm in the small meeting room, the big one is taken. Sorry, let me just close the door.
Much better. So, thanks for making the time. The idea today is simple. We want your new employees to give us everything once, so that you stop chasing them for
Yes, please. Right now it's a mess. I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand. Last month I spent a full a
Okay. And how many people do you hire in a year?
Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.
Good. Let's start with the biggest pain. What takes you the most time?
So who actually needs to answer them?
Okay, that's clear. And the questionnaire itself is what?
Great. Do you also want a photo? Some customers ask for one.
It could. Do you want that from day one?
We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call, that's easier than me explaining it.
Perfect. What do you need for the fund that you don't have?
Sorry, one second, someone's at my door. [pause] Okay, I'm back, sorry. Where were we?
The Julia story. It doesn't matter.
Right. What else about the employee affects the fund? Are they married, things like that?
And what are the options in that list?
Okay. Noted. Can I go back to source tax? You said all non-Swiss employees.
Sure, send it if it's easy. Do people need anything from you on the first day? Laptops, things like that? I just want to see if that belongs in the same form.
Okay. Anything else on who needs to do it? I'd rather hear all of it now.
Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.
Good. I'll send them after lunch. Thanks, Leo.

open_questions.question: Which questions does the Zurich source tax calculator ask to set the tariff code, with which options and under which conditions (including the different questions for married employees, such as whether the spouse works, and the extra questions and German forms for employees living abroad)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The source tax questions for subject employees cannot be specified; the calculator source has not been analysed yet. It may also need data not asked today (e.g. nationality of employees living abroad).
options: Analyse the Zurich calculator and add its questions, asked only when subject_to_source_tax is true
Release without source tax questions at first
open_questions.recommendation: Analyse the calculator before specifying the source tax step; ask its questions only to employees subject to source tax.

open_questions.question: Does the pension fund's 'Canton' mean the canton of residence or of work, and what should be entered for employees living abroad, given that only Swiss cantons are offered?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The canton is required for every registration; cross-border employees (e.g. living in Konstanz or Liechtenstein) cannot be registered without an answer.
options: Canton of residence; ask the fund what to use for employees living abroad
Canton of work (would not need to be asked of the employee, e.g. Zurich)
open_questions.recommendation: Ask Pensionskasse Muster. Until then, ask the canton only of employees living in Switzerland.

open_questions.question: How should an employee in a registered partnership (or other status not in the list, e.g. separated) be registered with the pension fund, does the fund want the partner's details, and does a registered partnership count as married for the source tax spouse rule?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The fund's civil status list has only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed; such employees cannot answer correctly and the source tax outcome may be wrong.
options: Ask the fund and HR and extend the list if the fund supports it
open_questions.recommendation: Ask Pensionskasse Muster; do not add values the fund does not accept.

open_questions.question: Does the pension fund portal show extra fields (e.g. spouse data) when civil status is Divorced or Widowed?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Missing a field would block registration for these employees.
options: Check the portal with these values
open_questions.recommendation: Ask HR for screenshots with Divorced and Widowed selected.

open_questions.question: Is the source tax rule complete? HR answered 'I think so' / 'I think that's it'.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Missing cases would ask the wrong people the source tax questions or skip people who must answer them.
open_questions.recommendation: Have HR confirm the decision table with a few real cases.

open_questions.question: Which permit types may the employee and spouse choose from? Sources mention only the B permit and the C permit.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The question needs a list of answers; only 'C permit' versus other matters for the source tax rule.
options: Get the list from HR or the calculator
Offer B permit, C permit and 'other'
open_questions.recommendation: Take the list from the Zurich calculator once analysed (OQ-01) or confirm with HR.

open_questions.question: Should the questionnaire remind employees to bring their permit, and with which wording?
open_questions.why_it_matters: HR wished for it because half of new employees forget; wording was deferred.
options: Add a reminder for employees with a permit
open_questions.recommendation: Decide with HR; a reminder for non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland seems natural.

open_questions.question: The Zurich calculator is used for every employee subject to source tax, though HR knows this is not exactly correct. Should this be revisited?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Known simplification agreed for now; may produce incorrect tariffs for employees in other cantons.
open_questions.recommendation: Keep for now as agreed and per the assignment's simplification.

Some rural or foreign addresses have no number, or use a building name. Should those employees be able to finish the step, for example by leaving the number empty or confirming 'no number'?

'No extra parts' (AC-02.1.2) rules out things like a c/o line, an apartment or flat number, or a second address line. Is that intended even when the post needs them to deliver (e.g. a new employee living c/o someone, or a large building abroad)? Or did HR only mean 'nothing beyond a normal envelope address'? This decides exactly which parts we collect.

AC-02.1.3 ('HR receives the complete home address' when 'the onboarding data is made available to the receiving parties') and AC-02.2.2 ('source tax and HR receive the country of residence') describe passing data on to other parties. out-of-scope.md (G-04) says that is a separate topic. What should these criteria be tested against in this feature? Should they be reworded to 'the information is collected and marked as needed by HR / source tax'?

What should happen if the employee goes back and changes the country after later steps were answered (e.g. Switzerland → Germany, or the reverse)? Should answers that no longer apply (nationality, canton, permit, spouse data) be discarded, which data minimisation (G-01) suggests? And should questions that now apply be asked again?

Which countries can the employee choose: any country in the world, or a limited list (e.g. Switzerland and neighbouring countries)? The examples confirm that Liechtenstein counts as 'abroad'. Is that confirmed by HR or the source tax office, given how closely Liechtenstein is tied to Switzerland?

Should address parts be checked for plausibility for the chosen country (e.g. a Swiss postcode must exist and match the town)? Or is any non-empty entry accepted? HR's need is mail that arrives, so wrong postcodes matter to them.
Does HR or the employer already know the employee's address before onboarding, so it could be pre-filled for the employee to confirm, or must the employee always type it in?

AC-02.2.4 only says the address step comes before the pension and source tax steps. Does it have to come at a particular place relative to FEAT-01 (first working day) or other steps, or is anything acceptable as long as it comes before the dependent steps?

The goal says a registration is "never blocked by missing data", but the fund requires a canton for every employee and US-03.4 skips the canton for anyone living abroad (Germany, Liechtenstein). Until OQ-02 is answered, these registrations will be blocked. For now, should Lonio still let these employees complete the questionnaire, or should the case be marked as incomplete or flagged to HR? Or do we accept that the goal is not met for them yet? This is separate from OQ-02 itself, which asks what the canton means.

For employees living in Switzerland, the canton follows from the Swiss postcode and town they already give in FEAT-02. Guidance prefers deriving values over asking for them. Should the canton be derived from the address instead of asked? If it is still asked, what happens when the chosen canton does not match the postcode? Should it be checked, or accepted as entered?

Suppose an employee answers a dependent question and then changes the answer it depends on: civil status from Married to something else, or country from Switzerland to abroad. Should the spouse's date of birth or canton they already gave be discarded? Data minimisation (G-01) suggests yes, but the spec does not say.

Which names should the employee enter: the official names exactly as on their passport or ID, including all first names and middle names, or the name they use day to day? The fund's registration and later matching may depend on this, and it changes the question wording and help text.

Are there plausibility rules for the employee's date of birth and the spouse's date of birth? For example: not in the future, a minimum or maximum age for the employee, the spouse being an adult. Today the only rules are "not empty" and "a valid date", so a mistyped year would reach the fund.

AC-03.1.3 ("another part of the onboarding or another receiving party needs the same detail … not asked again") cannot be tested as written. Which other features or parties reuse name and date of birth? The information catalogue lists only the pension fund. What should the test check?

The title of AC-03.2.3 says civil status is reused "for source tax and HR", but its Then clause covers only source tax. Is there an HR reuse that needs its own acceptance criterion? If not, should "HR" be removed from the title?

Where in the questionnaire flow does the canton question go? FEAT-02 (AC-02.2.3) says employees living in Switzerland "continue to nationality and canton" straight after the address. FEAT-03 groups name and date of birth under "personal details" and civil status under "family details" but does not place the canton. Is there a required order across FEAT-02, FEAT-03 and FEAT-04?

Who makes the source tax decision: Lonio automatically, or HR? AC-04.1.1, AC-04.2.1 and AC-04.3.1 say 'HR uses it to decide', but US-04.4 and AC-04.4.1–4 say Lonio decides and that this gates the tariff questions straight away. If Lonio decides, can HR review or override it (for example in a case the rule does not cover, OQ-05) before the employee gets or skips the source tax step?

Does the spouse rule apply to anyone other than civil status 'Married'? Registered partners (e.g. Daniel), separated spouses and anyone else outside the pension fund's 4 values would currently go straight to 'subject'. OQ-03 raises this for source tax but is not linked to this feature. Should FEAT-04 wait for it, or ship treating only 'Married' as married?

The rule only needs to know whether someone is Swiss, holds a C permit or lives in Switzerland. Should Lonio ask for the full nationality (employee and spouse) and the spouse's full country of residence, or only 'Swiss yes/no' and 'lives in Switzerland yes/no'? The 'What?' rows say '(whether they hold a Swiss passport)' / '(whether they live in Switzerland)', but the ACs say 'asks for the nationality' and 'asks where the spouse lives'. Under data minimisation (G-01) the answer changes what we collect. Does HR need the actual nationality for anything else?

How should dual nationals be handled? Is someone who holds Swiss and another nationality treated as Swiss, both for the employee and for the spouse? This decides whether one nationality answer is enough or several are allowed.

Permit type is required for every non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland. What should an employee answer if their permit is still being applied for or has not been issued yet, or if they hold something that is not a residence permit (e.g. a short-term or asylum status)? Can they finish the questionnaire, and what does the rule decide for them? This goes beyond OQ-06, which only covers the list of permit types.

'Lives in Switzerland' comes only from the country of the home address. What about weekly residents and others with two homes, e.g. a Swiss address during the week and a family home abroad? Which address should the employee give, and does HR accept that the rule follows it?

If the employee changes an earlier answer (address country, nationality, permit, civil status, spouse details) after the follow-up questions were answered, should the answers that are no longer needed be discarded (data minimisation), and should the source tax decision and the source tax step be recalculated? What happens to tariff answers already given if the employee turns out not to be subject?
Should the employee see the outcome (e.g. 'you are / are not subject to source tax'), or is it only stored for HR and the source tax step? No AC says who sees the decision or where.

AC-04.4.5 is a release precondition ('HR has checked the rules against real cases'), not behaviour we can test in the product, and its own trace check says the sources do not support it. Who signs this off, and is it a release gate for this feature or just part of resolving OQ-05?

Can a spouse who holds a C permit be living abroad (a C permit usually lapses after a long stay abroad)? If not, can we skip the residence question for C-permit spouses? Should the residence question be asked even when the spouse obviously lives with the employee?

already_flagged: OQ-01: Extra source tax calculator questions for employees living abroad (German forms etc.) are undefined, and the calculator may need the nationality of employees living abroad. This conflicts with AC-02.2.2, which says nationality is never asked of them.

OQ-02: Whether the pension fund 'Canton' means residence or work canton, and what to enter for employees living abroad. AC-02.2.2/AC-02.2.3 present 'canton not asked abroad' as final, but it is only the interim recommendation of OQ-02 (the trace check also notes it is not backed by the sources).
OQ-05: Completeness of the source tax rule that AC-02.2.2 relies on (living abroad → always subject).
OQ-02: whether the fund's Canton means the canton of residence or of work, and what to enter for employees living abroad (US-03.4, AC-03.4.1)
OQ-03: how to register employees in a registered partnership or another status such as separated, and whether the fund wants the partner's details (AC-03.2.2)
OQ-04: whether the portal shows extra spouse fields for Divorced or Widowed. The AC-03.3.1 example rows already mark these as 'not asked ✅' although the question is open

OQ-01: the Zurich calculator's tariff questions are undefined, including the questions for married employees and employees living abroad, and whether nationality is needed for employees living abroad (blocking; AC-04.1.2, AC-04.4.4)
OQ-05: HR is not sure the source tax rule is complete (AC-04.4.5)
OQ-06: full list of permit types for the employee and the spouse (AC-04.2.3, AC-04.3.2)
OQ-07: whether to add a reminder to bring the permit, and its wording (AC-04.2.3)
OQ-08: Zurich calculator used for every subject employee as an agreed simplification (AC-04.4.4)

tech_leaks.quote: they give the start date as currently agreed with Muster AG, as a full date in the form DD.MM.YYYY
tech_leaks.why: Sets the input format the employee must type. G-10 covers business wording for values in examples. The fund's DD.MM.YYYY requirement (F-SC-009) applies to the insurance start date sent to the fund, not to how the employee enters the first working day. How the date is entered (date picker, locale format) is a UI decision for engineering.

tech_leaks.quote: When they reach the employment details
tech_leaks.why: Assumes a questionnaire step called 'employment details' that no source asks for. How the questions are split into steps is a design choice.

tech_leaks.quote: When the onboarding data is made available to the receiving parties … Then HR receives the complete home address
tech_leaks.why: This describes how and when the system hands data over to recipients. Nobody asked for that behaviour here, and G-04 puts transmission out of scope. The business need is only that the address is collected once and is available for HR.

tech_leaks.quote: and cannot complete the step while any of these five parts is empty
tech_leaks.why: This prescribes how the form behaves (blocking the step). The business requirement is only that all five parts are required. How completeness is enforced (blocking, warning, review before submitting) is a design decision.

tech_leaks.quote: It depends on address_country from FEAT-02.
tech_leaks.why: Uses an internal field id in business prose. The business term is "country of home address".

tech_leaks.quote: naming the item residence_canton is an unbacked assumption
tech_leaks.why: Refers to an internal field or data-model name in the body text. What to call the field is an engineering decision.

tech_leaks.quote: they are asked for their date of birth as a day, month and year (shown as DD.MM.YYYY, e.g. 14.02.1990)
tech_leaks.why: The fund's DD.MM.YYYY format is a constraint on the data delivered to the fund. Telling the questionnaire to ask for day, month and year as separate parts and to display them that way is an input and UI decision that belongs to engineering and design.

tech_leaks.quote: Analyse the Zurich calculator and add its questions, asked only when subject_to_source_tax is true
tech_leaks.why: Uses an internal field id and a boolean value in prose. The business statement is 'asked only of employees subject to source tax'.

tech_leaks.quote: Lonio asks for the employee's nationality, the employee must answer it, and HR uses it to decide
tech_leaks.why: Says how the decision is made (a question that HR then uses) instead of what outcome is needed. It also conflicts with US-04.4, where Lonio itself decides. This is a borderline case: how the decision is handled internally should be left to the design.

review.summary: Not ready. All 58 examples pass, and item recall and precision are 1.0. Two open questions block release: OQ-01 (the Zurich source tax calculator was never analysed) and OQ-02 (what the pension fund's canton means). Some traceability is broken: FEAT-02 cites G-09 as confirmation, but G-09 is only the language rule, and AC-04.4.5 claims HR checked the rules, which no source supports. Several acceptance criteria describe passing data on to other parties, which G-04 puts out of scope. FEAT-04 contradicts itself on who decides source tax. Dev refinement left about 18 major questions. The biggest gaps are in FEAT-01, which comes from the Julia incident, and in FEAT-04. There are also 9 technical leaks. 14 inferred items or stories still need product owner confirmation.

findings.title: OQ-01 blocking: the source tax tariff questions are undefined
findings.why: The source tax step for employees who are subject to it can't be specified. The calculator may also need data the spec rules out, such as nationality for employees living abroad, which conflicts with AC-02.2.2.
findings.evidence: OQ-01 (blocking); skipped_sources: zh_source_tax_calculator; dev_refinement already_flagged (AC-02.2.2, AC-04.1.2, AC-04.4.4).
findings.action: Either analyse the Zurich calculator now, or record a decision in decisions.yaml to release FEAT-04 as the liability decision only, with no tariff step yet. Re-check AC-02.2.2 against the result.

findings.title: OQ-02 blocking: the canton's meaning is unknown, but the interim answer is written as final
findings.why: The fund requires a canton for every registration. Cross-border employees (Konstanz, Liechtenstein) can't be registered, which contradicts the FEAT-03 goal 'never blocked by missing data'. AC-02.2.2, AC-02.2.3 and US-03.4 treat 'canton not asked abroad' as settled.
findings.evidence: OQ-02; trace_judge partial on item.residence_canton, story.US-02.2 and story.US-03.4; FEAT-03 dev_refinement major question on the 'never blocked' goal.
findings.action: Ask Pensionskasse Muster whether it means canton of residence or of work, and what to enter for people living abroad. Until then, record in decisions.yaml how incomplete registrations are handled, for example flagged to HR. Mark the affected ACs as interim.

findings.title: Broken traceability: citations that confirm nothing
findings.why: The notes for the address country used as country of residence say this is confirmed by G-09, but G-09 is only 'Questionnaire language: English'. AC-04.4.5 claims HR checked the rules against real cases, which no source supports. Both make inferred items look confirmed when they aren't.
findings.evidence: FEAT-02 Notes (G-09); fact_judge partial F-TR-040; trace_judge partial story.US-04.4 (AC-04.4.5).
findings.action: Remove the false G-09 reference and either record a real decision on 'residence = country of home address' or raise an open question. Drop AC-04.4.5 or turn it into a sign-off step under OQ-05 with a named owner.

findings.title: Acceptance criteria test passing data on, which G-04 puts out of scope
findings.why: Engineering can't build or test criteria about how data reaches other parties when that handover is explicitly out of scope.
findings.evidence: AC-01.1.3, AC-02.1.3, AC-02.2.2 ('source tax and HR receive…'), AC-03.1.3; tech_leak FEAT-02; dev_refinement FEAT-01 and FEAT-02.
findings.action: Reword these to say the data is collected once and marked as needed by HR, the fund or source tax. Add guidance that features must not specify how data is passed on.

findings.title: FEAT-04 contradicts itself: who decides source tax liability?
findings.why: AC-04.1.1, AC-04.2.1 and AC-04.3.1 say 'HR uses it to decide', while US-04.4 says Lonio decides automatically and that this decision controls which questions follow. The flow and the option for HR to override depend on which is true.
findings.action: Record in decisions.yaml whether Lonio decides automatically and whether HR can review or override it, especially for cases OQ-05 doesn't cover. Align the ACs with that decision.

findings.title: FEAT-01 is underspecified on the very incident it is meant to prevent
findings.why: Several things are open. Is the first working day the contract start or the first day actually worked? Is it prefilled from HR or typed in by the employee? What happens if the date changes after onboarding, as in Julia's case? Which dates are allowed (past dates, typos)? Each of these can produce a wrong insurance start date again.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement FEAT-01 (4 major); fact_judge partial F-TR-014, F-TR-018, F-TR-019.
findings.action: Ask HR to clarify, then record decisions on: the definition of first working day, the source of the date (prefilled or typed), whether HR or the employee can change it after onboarding with the insurance start date recalculated, and the limits on allowed dates.

findings.title: The data collected for the source tax rule is not settled
findings.why: Unclear whether to collect full nationality or only 'Swiss yes/no' (data minimisation, G-01). Dual nationals, pending or unusual permits, and registered partners have no defined handling. OQ-03 is not linked to FEAT-04.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement FEAT-04 (4 major); OQ-03, OQ-06; eval: source_tax stakeholder missing on nationality, permit_type, spouse_nationality, spouse_permit_type, spouse_residence_country.
findings.action: Record decisions on how much nationality detail to collect, on dual nationals counting as Swiss, on pending permits, and on treating only 'Married' as married until OQ-03 is answered. Link OQ-03 to FEAT-04 and add source_tax as a stakeholder on these items.

findings.title: No rule for changing earlier answers or for the address details
findings.why: If an employee changes their country or civil status, the spec doesn't say whether dependent answers are discarded (G-01) or whether the decision is recalculated. The address also has gaps: a house number is always required, extra parts (c/o, flat) are excluded, and weekly residents aren't handled. Some employees may be unable to finish the address step.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement FEAT-02 (major: house number, extra parts, residence definition, country change); FEAT-03 (major: dependent data); FEAT-04 (minor).
findings.action: Add a cross-cutting guidance rule: answers that no longer apply are discarded and the decisions are recalculated. Confirm with HR how house number and c/o lines are handled, and which address weekly residents should give.

findings.title: Technical decisions leak into the spec
findings.why: Several criteria prescribe UI and data-model choices instead of business needs: DD.MM.YYYY input and separate day, month and year fields, an 'employment details' step, blocking the step until it's complete, and internal field ids (address_country, residence_canton, subject_to_source_tax) used in prose.
findings.evidence: tech_leak findings on FEAT-01 (2), FEAT-02 (2), FEAT-03 (3), FEAT-04 (1) and open-questions.md (1).
findings.action: Rewrite these in business terms, for example 'all five parts are required' and 'country of home address'. Add guidance that input formats and step layout are design decisions.

findings.title: Canton handling and the fund's open rules
findings.why: For Swiss residents the canton could be derived from the postcode, and guidance prefers deriving values over asking. The AC-03.3.1 examples mark Divorced and Widowed as 'not asked ✅' even though OQ-04 is still open. F-SC-020 (unknown error behaviour) is not used anywhere. F-SC-019 still describes the insurance start rule as open even though F-TR-018 settles it.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement FEAT-03 (major, canton derivation); OQ-04; coverage F-SC-019, F-SC-020.
findings.action: Decide whether to derive the canton or ask for it, and how to handle a canton that doesn't match the postcode. Ask HR for portal screenshots with Divorced and Widowed selected. Mark F-SC-019 as superseded by F-TR-018.
